label: rem:sniady-genus-grading-dimension-obstruction
title: Genus grading of character observables and the non-polynomiality of hook dimensions
html:
At the classical specialisation q = 1, where H_k(1) \cong \mathbb{C}[S_k], the non-vanishing third moment of the Blitvić-hypothesis proposition has its symmetric-group counterpart in the three-cycle character observable on Young diagrams \lambda \vdash k. Let \mathcal{A} denote the Kerov--Olshanski algebra of polynomial functions on Young diagrams, generated by the normalised conjugacy-class indicators \Sigma_{k_1, \dots, k_t} (or equivalently by the transition-measure free cumulants R_2, R_3, R_4, \dots). For any set partition \pi of an n-element set, Piotr Śniady proves that the partition-indexed indicator \Sigma_\pi \in \mathcal{A} has filtration degree

  \deg \Sigma_\pi = n - 2\,\mathrm{genus}_\pi

[sniady2006asymptotics, §3.1, Prop. 3.4], so non-crossing partitions (\mathrm{genus}_\pi = 0) govern the leading order and evercrossing partitions of genus 1 govern the first subleading correction to normalised characters and Jucys--Murphy free cumulants [sniady2006asymptotics, §4.5, Thms. 4.13--4.14]. In particular, the normalised three-cycle central character

  \omega_3(\lambda) = \frac{k(k-1)(k-2)\,\chi^\lambda((123))}{3\,f^\lambda} = \sum_{\square \in \lambda} c(\square)^2 - \binom{k}{2}

and the fourth free cumulant R_4(\lambda) = 3\,\omega_3(\lambda) - k both belong to \mathcal{A} in filtration degree 4, and under the Plancherel measure \mathbb{P}_{\mathrm{Planch}}(\lambda) = (f^\lambda)^2 / k! their expectations satisfy \mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{Planch}}[\omega_3] = 0 and \mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{Planch}}[R_4] = -k.

By contrast, the dimension-cubed three-cycle sum

  \sum_{\lambda \vdash k} (f^\lambda)^3\,\omega_3(\lambda)
  = \frac{k(k-1)(k-2)}{3} \sum_{\lambda \vdash k} (f^\lambda)^2\,\chi^\lambda((123))
  = k!\,\mathrm{Cov}_{\mathrm{Planch}}\bigl(f^\lambda,\, \omega_3(\lambda)\bigr)
  = \frac{k!}{3}\,\mathrm{Cov}_{\mathrm{Planch}}\bigl(f^\lambda,\, R_4(\lambda)\bigr)

weights \omega_3 \in \mathcal{A} by an additional factor of the hook-length dimension f^\lambda = k! / \prod_{\square \in \lambda} h(\square). Because f^\lambda grows on the scale \sqrt{k!} across typical Plancherel shapes rather than polynomially in the free cumulants (R_m)_{m \ge 2}, neither f^\lambda nor \ln f^\lambda lies in \mathcal{A}. Proposition~3.4 of [sniady2006asymptotics] grades Plancherel joint cumulants of elements within \mathcal{A}, so the genus filtration controls the \omega_3 factor in \mathrm{Cov}_{\mathrm{Planch}}(f^\lambda, R_4) without assigning a finite filtration degree or leading genus term to the product f^\lambda\,\omega_3(\lambda). Bounding the sign of \mathrm{Cov}_{\mathrm{Planch}}(f^\lambda, R_4) therefore requires a direct functional representation of f^\lambda or \ln f^\lambda over Young diagrams rather than finite-genus character asymptotics inside \mathcal{A}.
